# Incident Report — MTA 2026-02-28 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.2.28.88** | Conversation/DHCP/NBNS records |
| MAC | **00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.2.28.88`) and DHCP client hardware address, consistent across all frames |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR** | DHCP `dhcp.option.hostname`, corroborated by NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` name registration for 10.2.28.88 |
| AD domain | EASYAS123 (`easyas123.tech`, DC = EASYAS123-DC) | NBNS Local Master Browser `EASYAS123<1d>`; DNS SRV/LDAP queries to `_ldap._tcp....easyas123.tech` |
| Logged-in user | **brolf** | Kerberos `CNameString` field on AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic between 10.2.28.88 and the DC (10.2.28.2) |

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (commercial NetSupport Manager remote-control software abused as a backdoor/RAT).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The TCP payload of the beaconing stream is the literal NetSupport protocol, not just a suspicious pattern:

```
POST http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm HTTP/1.1
User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
...
CMD=POLL
INFO=1
ACK=1

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
...
CMD=ENCD
ES=1
DATA=<encrypted blob>
```

`CMD=POLL/ENCD`, the `NetSupport Manager/1.3` User-Agent, and the `NetSupport Gateway/1.92` server banner are the unmistakable NetSupport client/gateway handshake fields — this is a direct protocol match, not an inference from indirect behavior.

## Timeline / Infection Window
- Normal enterprise traffic (Kerberos, LDAP, SMB, Windows/Office telemetry) runs from capture start.
- t=44.44s: DNS query for `www.fmcsa.dot.gov`, immediately followed by a TLS session to 23.64.147.24 (SNI `www.fmcsa.dot.gov`).
- t=44.77s: DNS query for `vadusa.xyz` → resolves to 45.131.214.85.
- t=44.89s: TCP handshake to 45.131.214.85:443.
- t=45.05s: First `POST /fakeurl.htm` NetSupport RAT beacon (`CMD=POLL`).
- From that point through the end of the capture (~15,680s later), the host sends a NetSupport POLL/ENCD beacon roughly every 30–90 seconds — steady, persistent C2 traffic.

Note: the `fmcsa.dot.gov` session is TLS-encrypted, so the exact lure content (e.g., a fake-CAPTCHA/ClickFix-style page) is not visible in this capture, and no executable/script download precedes the beacon over HTTP — the RAT was already installed/running by the time it starts polling. The close timing to the fmcsa.dot.gov visit is a behavioral correlation only, not a confirmed delivery chain, and should be treated as investigative lead rather than proven fact.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **45.131.214.85:443** (plaintext HTTP over port 443 — TLS-evasion trick, no TLS handshake ever negotiated on this port) | `tcp.stream==40`, sustained POST beacon traffic, ~274 requests over the capture |
| Domain | **vadusa.xyz** | `dns.a==45.131.214.85`, DNS A-record query/response at t=44.77s |
| URL | **http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm** | HTTP request line on every beacon (frames 2638, 2639, 2640… through 15499) |
| Malicious User-Agent | **NetSupport Manager/1.3** | Present on every POST to the C2 |
| C2 server banner | **NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)** | Present on every HTTP 200 response from 45.131.214.85 |

No malware binary (installer/dropper/EXE/DLL/script) was transferred over the wire during this capture — every other file object exported from the pcap (`connecttest.txt`, Windows Update `.cab` files, OCSP responses, `msedge...filestreamingservice` blobs, `assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` from Adobe) resolves to legitimate Microsoft/Adobe update and telemetry infrastructure and is benign. Consequently there are no file-name or SHA256 IOCs to report for the RAT payload itself from this evidence — it must have arrived (or been staged) by a mechanism outside this capture's visibility.

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR** (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), logged in as domain user **brolf** on the EASYAS123 AD domain, began beaconing to **NetSupport RAT** command-and-control at **vadusa.xyz (45.131.214.85:443, plaintext HTTP)** roughly 45 seconds into the capture, shortly after a TLS session to `www.fmcsa.dot.gov`. The C2 channel uses the RAT's native POLL/ENCD protocol (`User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92`) over `/fakeurl.htm`, and remained active with regular polling for the remainder of the ~4.3-hour capture. Attribution to NetSupport RAT is signature-confirmed from the protocol fields themselves; the exact delivery/dropper mechanism is not visible in this evidence set.
